summary: Chips and AI hardware rebounded on Oct 21 after eight straight down sessions in the Philadelphia semiconductor index: the S&P 500 closed at 7,757.71 (+0.59%), the Nasdaq Composite at 26,702.86 (+1.05%) and the Dow at 52,856.09 (+0.69%), with the VIX at 16.68 and the 10-year yield at 5.15%. Samsung rose 5.7% and SK hynix 5.8% on the day but remain down 3.7% and 8.8% on the week, while Taiwan's MediaTek is down 7.5% on the week. Brent settled at 108.82 and WTI at 97.15 after Brent briefly topped $110 on stalled US-Iran talks; Indonesia's EIDO rose 2.2% on the day but is down 9.8% on the week. Bank Indonesia held its rate on Oct 21, and Bank of Korea and BSP decisions on Oct 22 fall after the data date. Several commodity, freight and policy-rate items could not be refreshed (see gaps).

indicators.name: TSMC monthly revenue

checks.name: stated change matches values on file

indicators.name: Korea semiconductor exports
indicators.source_name: Korea Times and Korea JoongAng Daily, quoting the ministry release
indicators.note: Released on the 1st. Mostly read from news reports of the ministry release unless the release itself is found; the ministry's English name changes between outlets.

indicators.name: Japan-made chip equipment billings

checks.name: stated change matches values on file

indicators.note: Semiconductor equipment only. SEAJ also publishes flat panel display equipment with a near-identical title; do not use that report. Figures are 3-month averages, and the first release of a month is preliminary.

indicators.name: Global chip equipment billings

checks.name: stated change matches values on file

indicators.note: Quarterly, released about three months after the quarter ends. Regional tables are images, so only the global total is recorded.

indicators.name: Global semiconductor sales

checks.name: stated change matches values on file

indicators.note: 3-month moving average of monthly sales. Earlier months are revised in later releases, so revisions are stored as new rows.

indicators.name: FAO Food Price Index
indicators.note: Published the first Friday of the month on fao.org. The previous month is often revised, so enter any restated value again.

indicators.name: FAO cereals sub-index
indicators.note: Same FAO release as the headline index.

indicators.name: FAO vegetable oils sub-index
indicators.note: Same FAO release as the headline index.

indicators.name: FAO sugar sub-index
indicators.note: Same FAO release as the headline index.

indicators.name: US corn ending stocks, 2026/27 projection
indicators.note: World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates, about the 10th. The projected marketing year rolls over each September, so month-on-month change compares like with like only within a year.

indicators.name: US rotary rig count (Baker Hughes)
indicators.note: Published Fridays. The release is reached through press reports quoting Baker Hughes, so tier stays reported unless the Baker Hughes page itself is reachable.

indicators.name: US working gas in storage (EIA)
indicators.note: Thursday release for the week ending the prior Friday. The EIA page can return an old cached copy: check that its week-ending date matches the period before recording a value.

indicators.name: Refined copper market balance, year to date (ICSG)
indicators.note: Positive is surplus, negative is deficit, cumulative within the year. Reached through press reports quoting ICSG.

indicators.name: US reactors at 0% power (NRC daily report)
indicators.note: Count of units shown at 0% on the Friday daily report at nrc.gov (URL pattern .../reactor-status/2026/YYYYMMDDps.html). Autumn refuelling pushes the count up. Counted from the page text, so check the count against the page.

indicators.name: Uranium spot price, month-end (Cameco)
indicators.note: Cameco's page lists the month-end spot and long-term price; the long-term price is kept in the note.

spreads.name: Brent minus WTI
spreads.note: Gap between the two main crude benchmarks.

spreads.name: Copper to aluminum price ratio
spreads.note: Copper in USD per tonne (pounds converted) divided by aluminum in USD per tonne.

spreads.name: Copper to gold ratio
spreads.note: Copper USD per pound divided by gold USD per ounce, times 1000. A familiar growth-versus-safety gauge.
